correctness.rationale: For all integers m,n>=5, the eight-shift eigenvalue is exactly 4(cos(theta)+cos(phi))(2cos(theta)cos(phi)-1). The first factor contributes 2g*1_{2|lcm}-1_{2|m}-1_{2|n}, via exact homomorphism fiber intersections. The two-term rational-cosine theorem of Conway and Jones, Acta Arith. 30 (1976), Theorem 7, restricts the second factor to the four order-six and eight order-eight angular families, giving the remaining indicator terms without overlap. An exact independent finite-field evaluator reproduces the nullities in all 400 rectangular sizes 5..24 and seven boundary cases. Numerical checks corroborate, but are not substituted for, the full proof.

originality.rationale: The closest accessible graph-specific primary article, Cibu et al., The Gonality of Chess Graphs (arXiv:2403.03907, original 2024-03-06), studies chip-firing gonality rather than the complex adjacency nullity. Theorem 7 of Conway-Jones (1976) supplies a classical classification of two-angle trigonometric relations but neither defines this toroidal knight operator nor counts the null eigencharacters. John and Sachs (Discrete Mathematics 309, 2009) give periodic-graph spectral methods, including toroidal hexagonal illustrations, but no identified result states or directly specializes to the full m-by-n knight nullity formula. This is a best-knowledge claim, subject to older specialized knight-board spectral tables.

The invertibility if and only if both sides are odd and the independent six- and eight-torsion corrections are sharp structural resonances rather than an arbitrary finite calculation.
